# 01 geo index -- the existing Doris index already does C.1/C.2 (MEASURED)

MEASURED 2026-11-19T18:05Z on the plan-01 B.2 cluster (c05, master dbb9b19391 + plan commits, RELEASE),
with `h3_lat_lng_to_cell` standing in for `s2_cell` (same shape: BIGINT from lat/lon; the running binary
predates s2_cell).

## 1. Generated cell column + numeric inverted index: works today, no FE/BE change
```sql
CREATE TABLE geo.gc_probe (id BIGINT NOT NULL, lon DOUBLE NOT NULL, lat DOUBLE NOT NULL,
  cell BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (h3_lat_lng_to_cell(lat, lon, 9)),
  INDEX idx_cell (cell) USING INVERTED)
DUPLICATE KEY(id) DISTRIBUTED BY HASH(id) BUCKETS 4 PROPERTIES("replication_num"="1");
INSERT INTO geo.gc_probe (id, lon, lat) SELECT id, lon, lat FROM geo.geo_pts WHERE id < 100000;
```
100,000 rows loaded in 195 ms; `count(cell)` = 100,000.  The writer (plan 01 C.1) is the stock BKD
inverted-index writer: every segment gets a BKD tree on `cell` at load.  Nothing to build.

## 2. Range lookup prunes exactly -- once the BKD bypass heuristic is off
Query: `count(*) where cell between <p50> and <p51>` (1,001 hits of 100,000 rows), 4 segments.

| inverted_index_skip_threshold | RowsInvertedIndexFiltered | InvertedIndexDowngradeCount | ScanRows | RowsVectorPredFiltered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 (default) | 12,589 | 7 | 87,411 | 86,410 |
| 0 | 98,999 | 0 | **1,001** | 0 |

- Cause (`be/src/storage/index/inverted/inverted_index_iterator.cpp:91-107`): for a BKD reader the
  iterator first counts the hits (`try_read_from_inverted_index`) and BYPASSES the index when the count is
  above `inverted_index_skip_threshold`% (default 50) of the segment's rows.  It downgraded 7 of the
  predicate evaluations here.  An `OR` of many `BETWEEN`s is evaluated range by range, so a range whose
  count is wrongly estimated trips the bypass.
- With the bypass off, ScanRows == hits: the reader (plan 01 C.2 "polygon -> row bitmap") is the stock BKD
  range query.  A polygon query = `(cell BETWEEN lo1 AND hi1 OR ...) AND ST_Contains(...)`, with the ranges
  from `geo_index::cover()` and Doris' own `ST_Contains` as the exact recheck.

## Consequences for plan 01 Phase C (KISS)
- C.1 writer: no new code.  DDL only: generated column `s2_cell(lat, lon)` + `INDEX ... USING INVERTED`.
- C.2 reader: no new index reader.  The new work is the planner rewrite: constant polygon -> cover() ranges
  -> OR of BETWEEN on the cell column, AND the original ST_Contains.
- The rewrite must keep the BKD index in use: either (a) set `inverted_index_skip_threshold = 0` for the
  rewritten predicate (session-level today; per-predicate needs a change), or (b) a single
  `cell IN RANGES(...)` predicate the BKD reader evaluates as one union (no per-range bypass).
  Pick by measurement in C.3 (KISS: (a) first).

## 3. C.3a measured: s2_covers(geo_cell, poly) AND ST_Contains on 10 M rows (2026-11-19T19:20Z)

Table `geo.geo_pts_idx` = the B.2 dataset + `geo_cell BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (s2_cell(lat, lon))` +
`INDEX idx_cell (geo_cell) USING INVERTED` (storage format V3 = SNII BKD).  Load of 10 M rows: 2.5 s
(B.2 without the column: 4.6 s on a cold cluster -- the generated column + BKD index add no visible
load cost here).  RELEASE build of the C.3a working tree, caches off, 1 cold + median of 3 warm.

| polygon | mode | hits | rows scanned | RowsInvertedIndexFiltered | warm ms | cold ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| city | full (no index) | 273,872 | 10,000,000 | 0 | 222 | 340 |
| city | s2_covers + ST_Contains | 273,872 | **334,307** | 9,665,693 | **75** | 575 |
| thin | full (no index) | 76,897 | 10,000,000 | 0 | 233 | 242 |
| thin | s2_covers + ST_Contains | 76,897 | **454,646** | 9,545,354 | **74** | 1,816 |
| concave | full (no index) | 1,001,100 | 10,000,000 | 0 | 227 | 238 |
| concave | s2_covers + ST_Contains | 1,001,100 | **1,466,496** | 8,533,504 | **118** | 1,053 |

- Correct: hits are identical to the unindexed `ST_Contains` for all three polygons (G3 on this data).
  The planar-bbox prefilter lost 83 city hits (01.geo.baseline.md); the S2 cover does not.
- Pruning: city scans 3.3% of rows (G4 bar <= 5%: PASS at 10 M), candidate/hit 1.22; thin 5.9x, concave 1.46x.
- Warm: 3.0x (city), 3.1x (thin), 1.9x (concave) faster than the full scan.  Versus the planar bbox (B.3: city 62,
  thin 172, concave 97 ms), the index wins for thin (2.3x) but not yet for city or concave.
- Cold is SLOW (575-1,816 ms).  Cause (audit `gpt-6-astra`, finding 1 of 02.audit.be-adapter.md round 2):
  each cover range is two ONE-SIDED BKD queries (`>= lo`, `<= hi`), each materialising about half the
  segment's doc ids before the AND: 2 x ranges x rows of work.  The warm runs are fast only because the
  InvertedIndexQueryCache keeps those half-segment bitmaps.
- Fix (plan 01 C.4): one BOUNDED query per range.  `snii::bkd::BkdReader::range(lower, upper)` already exists
  (`be/src/storage/index/inverted/snii/bkd/bkd_reader.h:79`); `build_bkd_query_bounds` only maps the
  five one-sided/equal query types.  Expected: cold ~ warm, and work ~ candidates instead of ~ rows.

## 4. C.4 measured: one bounded BETWEEN_QUERY per cover range (2026-11-19T20:20Z)

Same table and queries as section 3, with `enable_inverted_index_query_cache = false`, so EVERY run is
"cold" for the index (section 3's cold numbers were the honest cost; its warm numbers came from the cache).

| polygon | mode | hits | rows scanned | warm ms | cold ms | C.3a cold ms (one-sided scans) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| city | full (no index) | 273,872 | 10,000,000 | 200 | 300 | 340 |
| city | s2_covers + ST_Contains | 273,872 | 334,307 | **69** | **105** | 575 |
| thin | full (no index) | 76,897 | 10,000,000 | 232 | 296 | 242 |
| thin | s2_covers + ST_Contains | 76,897 | 454,646 | **67** | **109** | 1,816 |
| concave | full (no index) | 1,001,100 | 10,000,000 | 223 | 267 | 238 |
| concave | s2_covers + ST_Contains | 1,001,100 | 1,466,496 | **110** | **148** | 1,053 |

- city index time: InvertedIndexSearcherSearchTime 2.8-3.2 ms (was 370 ms) -- the bounded traversal reads
  only the leaves inside each cover range.  Cold is now 1.4-1.6x warm (C.4 bar: <= 2x, PASS).
- Hits unchanged for all three polygons (equal to the unindexed ST_Contains).
- city warm 69 ms vs the planar bbox 62 ms (B.3): not yet below it (C.4 bar <= 62 ms).  Profile: index 3 ms,
  ExprFilterEvalTime 8-10 ms; most of the rest is the per-block re-parse of the WKT polygon in `s2_covers`'
  row path and ST_Contains.  Next: cache the parsed polygon/ranges per FunctionContext (C.5), as
  ST_Contains already does (`StRelationState`).

## 5. Back-to-back medians, profile OFF (2026-11-19T20:30Z) -- supersedes the "69 ms" in section 4

Section 4's warm numbers were medians of 3 with `enable_profile = true` (profile collection costs ~10-15 ms
per query at this size).  Same cluster, profile off, all caches off incl. the inverted-index query cache,
median of 10 runs after 2 warm-up runs:

| polygon | full ST_Contains | planar bbox + ST_Contains (B.3) | s2_covers + ST_Contains | index vs full | index vs bbox |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| city | 188 ms | 57 ms (WRONG: 273,789 hits, 83 lost) | **51 ms** (273,872 hits) | 3.7x | 1.1x |
| thin | 217 ms | 170 ms | **56 ms** | 3.9x | 3.0x |
| concave | 214 ms | 92 ms | 97 ms | 2.2x | 0.95x |

- Floor: `select count(*) ... where id < 0` = 36 ms on this 16-bucket table (scan setup).  So city's real
  filter work is 51 - 36 = 15 ms, against 152 ms for the full scan.
- Decomposition (city): `s2_covers` alone 49 ms, + ST_Contains 56 ms -> the exact recheck of 334 k candidates
  adds ~7 ms; polygon parsing is not the bottleneck.  So C.5 (per-FunctionContext polygon cache) has no
  measurable target: dropped per R-KISS.
- The bbox is not a correct alternative (it loses geodesic hits), so the fair comparison is against the full
  scan: 2.2-3.9x at 10 M rows.  Concave equals the bbox because its U-shape bbox is tight and its cover has
  1.46x candidates; G4 (>= 3x vs bbox at 100 M) is measured in Z.3.

## 6. C.3b: plain ST_Contains is rewritten automatically (2026-11-19T21:20Z)

FE rule `GeoIndexRewrite` adds `s2_covers(geo_cell, '<wkt>')` next to `ST_Contains(ST_Polygon('<wkt>'),
ST_Point(lon, lat))` when the table has an inverted-indexed BIGINT column generated exactly as
`s2_cell(lat, lon)`.  The user's SQL does not change.  `EXPLAIN` of the unchanged query on `geo_pts_idx`:
```
0:VOlapScanNode(40)
   PREDICATES: (st_contains(st_polygon('POLYGON((116.20 39.75, ...))'), st_point(lon[#1], lat[#2]))
               AND s2_covers(geo_cell[#3], 'POLYGON((116.20 39.75, ...))'))
```
Same SQL `select count(*) from T where st_contains(st_polygon(W), st_point(lon, lat))`, all caches off,
median of 20 after the FE warm-up, 2 rounds:

| polygon | T = geo_pts (no cell column) | T = geo_pts_idx (rewritten) | speedup | hits (both tables) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| city | 180-185 ms | 48-58 ms | 3.2-3.8x | 273,872 |
| thin | 215-217 ms | 55-59 ms | 3.7-3.9x | 76,897 |
| concave | 203-211 ms | 96-97 ms | 2.1-2.2x | 1,001,100 |

The first ~10 queries after an FE restart run ~30 ms slower (cold FE / JIT); the numbers above exclude them.
